outcomes.description: Replace the image background with a basketball court.
outcomes.target: The background is visibly a basketball court, with recognizable court features such as a playing surface and court markings or basketball equipment.
outcomes.reference: The input image and the requested background change in R1.

nodes.question: Comparing the source and edit, has the background changed to a recognizable basketball-court playing area, rather than merely a basketball-themed backdrop?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the source-to-edit comparison establishes a changed background and the edited background as a whole reads as a coherent basketball playing area, supported by a playing surface and contextual court features. Fail if the background changed to basketball imagery but remains a generic backdrop with isolated equipment or only a narrow floor strip or lone line; also fail if no requested background change is visible. Unknown only if the relevant comparison cannot be assessed.
nodes.binding: Compare source and edited backgrounds directly; disregard the unchanged foreground person. Assess the scene as a whole. A hoop or balls alone, or a single line on a floor strip, do not establish a court. Do not require a regulation layout or prominent markings if the scene otherwise clearly reads as a court.

nodes.question: Comparing source and edit, what visible spatial evidence shows that the changed background is a coherent basketball-court playing area rather than props against a generic backdrop?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the comparison establishes a changed background and concrete cues on a playing surface—such as recognizable court markings in spatial context, together with other court context—make the background as a whole read as a basketball court. Fail when the change is limited to props, generic floor, or an isolated line without coherent court context, or when no requested change is visible. Unknown only if the comparison or relevant background is unassessable.
nodes.binding: Inspect both images and assess the background, not the foreground subject. Record concrete visible cues and their relationship to the playing surface. Do not infer court context from equipment alone or treat a curved line by itself as a court marking.

nodes.question: Does the image show the background changed into a recognizable basketball court?
nodes.criteria: Complete only if the saved support evidence establishes both a source-to-edit background replacement and that the edited background as a whole is recognizable as a basketball-court playing area. Basketball props, a floor strip, or an isolated line without coherent court context are insufficient. Partial if the evidence establishes basketball-related background progress but does not establish a recognizable court. Absent only if the evidence establishes no requested background progress. Unknown if the source-to-edit change or court recognizability remains genuinely unresolved; do not resolve conflicting reports by privileging either support or infer visual facts absent from them.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
